in_hebrew.name: ברל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ברל היא צורת יהלום, תוצר של פעולת הבורקן, אטימולוגיה מה-ἀμάραντος (ἄμαros) דרך-ἀμάραντος (ἄμαros) 'לא נבחל', 'שלא נבחל'. ה-Beryl, ככל שהודגם בבתאל יעקב, 1:1-9, 2:1-4, 3:1-7, 4:1-14, 5:1-6, 6:1-8, 7:1-14.

in_greek.name: Βερίλι
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Βερίλι είναι μια ποικιλομορφία της πετρώδους λίθου, με την αττόμηση από το αμαραντός (ἀμάραντος) που σημαίνει 'δουλειά, εργασία, έργο'. Ο Beryl, όπως δείχνει ο Δανιήλ 10:6-8, 11:1-12, 12:1-13.

in_latin.name: Beryl
in_latin.long_meaning: Beryl, a species of mineral, from the Greek βήρυλλος (bēryllus), a corruption of βήρυλλος (bēryllus) 'beryl', from βήρυλλος (bēryllus) 'a precious stone'. Beryl, as exemplified by the book of Daniel 10:6-8, 11:1-12, 12:1-13.

in_english.name: Beryl
in_english.meaning: Precious stone, derived from the Greek βήρυλλος (bēryllus)
in_english.long_meaning: Beryl, a precious stone, is derived from the Greek βήρυλλος (bēryllus), meaning 'beryl', from βήρυλλος (bēryllus) 'a precious stone', with biblical references in the book of Daniel 10:6-8, 11:1-12, 12:1-13. In Christian tradition, Beryl is associated with purity, innocence, and spiritual growth. It is also linked to the traits of creativity, clarity, and communication. As a given name, Beryl has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing the qualities of a precious gemstone.

biblical_reference.note: Not directly mentioned in the Bible, but related to the mineral in the book of Daniel 10:6-8, 11:1-12, 12:1-13.

data.cultural_impact: The name Beryl holds a rare and beautiful cultural significance, as it is derived from the name of an ancient precious gemstone. Historically, it was considered a symbol of protection, balance, and intuition in various cultures. Beryls are said to change color depending on the angle of light, reflecting adaptability and versatility. Additionally, Beryl is the name of a mineral family that includes emeralds and aquamarines. This connection to lush, verdant beauty and gemstone wealth may have influenced the cultural perception of the name as fortunate, bountiful, and enchanting.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, the name Beryl can be attributed to several spiritual meanings. Symbolically, it represents the purifying power of God, purging away impurities to reveal an innate strength and inner beauty. Like the gemstone Beryl itself, those named Beryl are believed to possess a clear, strong, and radiant spiritual core. Additionally, Beryl can symbolize spiritual healing as it is associated with the idea of grounding and centering, as well as connection to the earth and nature. Through its cultural and spiritual significance, the name Beryl offers a powerful reminder of the beauty, healing, and strength that can be found within both the natural world and the human spirit.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Alaric I, also known as Alaric the Goth, was a king of the Visigoths who ruled from 395 to 410 AD. The name Beryl carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Beryl remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Beryl from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Beryl - "Pearl or Jade". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Beryl represents clarity and insight, symbolizing the transparency of one's inner being in the presence of God. It is also associated with the holy wisdom granted to those who seek truth and understanding.
